document.executive_summary: Independent verification of the WO-01 pump-module decision. Recomputation from the trusted table confirms all four candidates qualify: quality indices 84/97/80/81 all meet the floor of 80, and defect counts 4/1/3/0 all sit at or below the ceiling of five. On the shared acceptance-run basis, measured energy ranks P2 first at 12 kWh, then P3 (52), P1 (56) and P4 (58). The lowest-energy qualifying package is therefore P2, and my independent ballot is P2. A's figures match the sources exactly; its delivered prose shows truncation and garbling, recorded below as presentation defects that do not alter the decision.
document.figure_caption: Verification panel: recomputed acceptance-run energy per candidate with the P2 dashed reference, plus eligibility gates showing quality margins above the 80 floor and defect counts against the 5 ceiling.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies cleanly (quality 97, one defect) and posts the lowest measured energy at 12 kWh per acceptance run, 40 kWh below runner-up P3 and 46 below P4. The client policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package, so P2 is the client winner on the supplied facts; my independent ballot is P2.

sections.body: The trusted table yields four passing profiles. Quality floor 80: P1 84 (margin +4), P2 97 (+17), P3 80 (+0), P4 81 (+1). Defect ceiling 5: P1 4 (headroom 1), P2 1 (4), P3 3 (2), P4 0 (5). Every module clears both gates, so eligibility does not separate the field. Two margins deserve audit before award: P3 sits exactly on the quality floor, so any downward correction of its index would disqualify it; P4's zero-defect count should be traced to raw inspection logs to rule out under-reporting. No candidate fails, and reject_all is unavailable on this data.
sections.heading: Eligibility Recomputation from Trusted Records

sections.body: Energy is the sole decision variable. Recomputed from the trusted measurements on the shared fixed flow and head basis: P2 12 kWh, P3 52, P1 56, P4 58. Gaps against the leader are P3 +40, P1 +44, P4 +46 kWh per acceptance run. Savings shares check: 12 kWh is 76.9% below P3, 78.6% below P1 and 79.3% below P4, so A's stated roughly 77–79% is correct rounding. P3's own gap is 4.33 times P2's consumption, so the lowest-energy rule resolves unambiguously to P2. No arithmetic on the register can reorder this ranking; there are no ties, so the ID tiebreak is not exercised.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Gap Verification

sections.body: A's delivered report matches the trusted table on every figure: all four quality indices, defect counts and energies are transcribed correctly, and the gap arithmetic is right. However, the prose is mechanically damaged: the P4 section ends mid-word, open question 5 is garbled, and the final paragraph is cut off mid-sentence. The claimed six open questions are only partly legible in the delivered pages. These are presentation defects, not measurement errors; they do not change the recommendation, but they should be logged in the assurance record for the next analyst.
sections.heading: Accuracy Check of A's Delivered Report

sections.body: Measured facts: the four quality, defect and energy records on one common test basis. Unverified, per the register: unit cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability for all candidates. One acceptance run cannot establish wear behavior in a reclamation loop. P4's zero-defect profile is a genuine robustness signal a risk-weighted client might weigh, but the stated policy is unambiguous and no supplied data supports overriding it. P2's high quality index of 97 rests on a single sampling method that deserves a method check. My verification found no basis to revise A's ranking.
sections.heading: Measured Facts, Open Questions and Residual Risk

body.figure_brief: Supporting illustration for the WO-01 pump-module verification memo. Render a clean two-panel analytical chart, no decorative imagery. Left panel: horizontal bars of measured acceptance-run energy per candidate on the shared duty basis — P2 12 kWh (highlighted green, labeled leader), P3 52, P1 56, P4 58 kWh — with a dashed vertical reference at the 12 kWh leader line and per-bar gap annotations (+40, +44, +46 kWh vs P2). Right panel: two small gate charts. Chart 1: quality indices 84/97/80/81 as bars against a dashed floor line at 80, noting P3 sits exactly on the floor. Chart 2: raw defect counts 4/1/3/0 as bars against a dashed ceiling line at 5, noting P1 has one defect of headroom and P4 has zero defects. Neutral engineering palette (slate blue bars, green highlight for P2, red dashed limit lines), sans-serif labels, clear axis ticks, no JavaScript. Purpose: show the verifier-recomputed ranking, the magnitude of the P2 energy advantage, and that eligibility gates do not separate the field.
